input_contract.description: Two triggers, both from a live paid session. Next-repair: a completed run. Make-good: a report that both AI authors declined, carrying token + machine identity.

output_contract.description: A single-use coupon code, or an honest no-op. Absent Stripe keys degrade gracefully to ok with couponCode null - never a fabricated code, never a blocked run.

observation_contract.description: Loyalty attaches AFTER the service and never affects it: it authors no plan, gates no state, blocks nothing. The make-good is the honest terminal recourse on AI failure (not a non-AI plan); the next-repair coupon is presented, never pushed (no-force ethos). The Custodian may PRESENT a coupon, but the coupon itself is minted only here.

evidence_contract.description: Coupons are real Stripe promotion codes (single-use), tagged with email + machine metadata; the make-good also sends the customer email + a Support incident. The issued code is the after-the-fact evidence of the honest recourse.

working_parameters.outside_parameters_behavior: Missing Stripe/Resend keys -> ok with couponCode null (honest no-op), never a fabricated code. A make-good is idempotent per session. No loyalty path can block, gate, or delay the paid repair flow.
